target_customer: Companies and engineering teams with growing multi-provider AI spend, including AI-native startups
problem: AI spend is scattered across provider consoles with no way to trace cost to customer, feature, team or pull request.
business_model: SaaS with freemium tiers for AI cost tracking and attribution (product name SuperPenguin)

founders.name: Christopher Acker
founders.background_notes: Launch post says he led AI at Skylo; the YC page does not confirm it is the same person.

founders.name: Yuta Baba
founders.background_notes: Senior data scientist at Snowflake leading ML bookings forecasts, per the YC page.

competitors.name: Helicone
competitors.what: LLM gateway logging cost per request with header-based attribution

competitors.name: Langfuse
competitors.what: Open source trace-level LLM observability with token cost per generation

competitors.name: CloudZero
competitors.what: Unit economics cost platform mapping cloud and AI spend to products and customers

competitors.name: Vantage and Finout
competitors.what: Cloud cost platforms expanding to AI providers

technical_complexity.rationale: Pulling billing from provider APIs and tagging requests with a thin SDK is mostly integration work; per-PR attribution via Cursor is the harder piece.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations are copyable and observability and FinOps vendors were adding the same views.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established FinOps vendors already listed AI cost tracking in 2026 comparison guides.

market_need_then: CloudZero's 2025 report, cited on its blog, puts average monthly enterprise AI spend at about $85.5K, up 36 percent year over year, supporting demand for visibility.

branding.domain_note: Product uses superpenguin.ai; legal company name Carrot Labs differs from the product brand

identity.logo: A penguin logo per the site; no description of meaning
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and direct: Know where your AI spend goes

branding.brand_signature: Penguin logo and the line 'Your providers tell you the total. We tell you what it was for.'
branding.community_and_virality: Listed on Product Hunt, PeerPush and BetaList; no organic fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable product name and penguin logo, but a split between Carrot Labs and SuperPenguin and no press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Carrot Labs, operating the SuperPenguin product, is an active Winter 2026 company tracking AI spend across 14 providers with one named customer, Channel3. It is early, funding is unverified, and established FinOps and LLM observability vendors already cover similar ground, so its outcome is undetermined.
notes: Unverified funding: Standout and CB Insights list $500K (convertible note, YC investor); Dealroom lists a $125k seed; all aggregators, so no round is recorded. A $600K seed for a different Carrot Labs (crypto lending) was excluded. Founded year not stated. Competitor sources are 2026 vendor roundups.
